question: The line \(y=-x+3\) intersects the x-axis at \((3,0)\), and \(y\) decreases as \(x\) increases. The solution set of the inequality \(-x+3<0\) is ( ).
solution: \(y<0\) corresponds to the graph being below the x-axis. Since \(y\) decreases as \(x\) increases, this occurs to the right of the intersection, that is, \(x>3\).

reference.question: The line \(y=-x+3\) intersects the x-axis at \((3,0)\), and \(y\) decreases as \(x\) increases. The solution set of the inequality \(-x+3<0\) is ( ).
reference.solution:
Method 1: Read the negative side of the intercept

\(y<0\) corresponds to the graph being below the x-axis. Since \(y\) decreases as \(x\) increases, this occurs to the right of the intersection, that is, \(x>3\).

Method 2: Solve using the negative coefficient

To isolate \(x\), subtract \(3\) from both sides of \(-x+3<0\), giving \(-x<-3\). Dividing both sides by \(-1\) reverses the inequality. Therefore the solution set is \(x>3\), with \(x=3\) excluded, choice C.
